claims.text: In a SELECT statement, the SELECT list names the output columns, FROM names the table, WHERE gives a condition rows must satisfy, ORDER BY sorts, LIMIT caps the number of rows returned; a statement ends with ; in psql.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs, SQL Commands: SELECT (Synopsis, Description); psql docs (commands end with semicolon)

claims.text: psql is PostgreSQL's terminal client; it sends queries to the server and prints results. In the lab it runs inside the lab box, a separate machine scripts/up.sh starts, which sees the repository at /repo; scripts/sql/run-query.sh re-runs itself there through its lab-run.sh line (l.5).
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs, psql reference (Description); examples/don-hang@stage-0: docker-compose.yml (lab volumes ./:/repo:ro), scripts/sql/run-query.sh l.5, scripts/lab-run.sh

claims.text: The clauses are written SELECT, FROM, WHERE, ORDER BY, LIMIT, but take effect in this order: FROM, WHERE, the SELECT output expressions, ORDER BY, then LIMIT returns a subset of the sorted rows. This is the result to match; PostgreSQL's actual steps may differ.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs, SQL Commands: SELECT, Description ('general processing of SELECT', steps FROM, WHERE, output, ORDER BY, LIMIT)

claims.text: WHERE keeps a row only if its condition is true; a row whose condition is false or null is discarded.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs §7.2.2 The WHERE Clause

claims.text: <> is SQL's not-equal operator. Ordinary comparison operators such as = and <> yield null (unknown), not true or false, when either input is null; e.g. 7 <> NULL yields null. Hence NULL = NULL yields null, not false.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs §9.2 Comparison Functions and Operators

claims.text: NULL stands for a value that is unknown or missing; it is different from zero and from an empty string.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs §9.2 (null signifies unknown); Appendix M Glossary: Null

claims.text: ORDER BY ... DESC sorts from largest to smallest; ASC (smallest first) is the default when neither is written.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs §7.5 Sorting Rows

claims.text: Without ORDER BY, rows come back in an unspecified order that depends on how PostgreSQL reads the table and the order on disk, and must not be relied on; LIMIT without ORDER BY gives an unpredictable subset.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs §7.5 Sorting Rows; §7.6 LIMIT and OFFSET

claims.text: A query does not say how to find the rows; PostgreSQL works out its own steps (a query plan) for each query, which must produce the rows the query describes.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs §14.1 Using EXPLAIN ('PostgreSQL devises a query plan for each query it receives')

claims.text: Every column in Đơn Hàng's tables at stage-0 is NOT NULL, either declared so or made so by its PRIMARY KEY (a primary key forces NOT NULL), so PostgreSQL refuses to store NULL in any of them.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang@stage-0: db/schema.sql (all CREATE TABLE statements); PostgreSQL 17 docs §5.5 Constraints (primary key forces NOT NULL)

claims.text: AS after an output expression gives that output column a name (column label), as in NULL IS NULL AS "null_is_null".
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs §7.3.2 Column Labels

claims.text: scripts/sql/run-query.sh runs db/queries/select-basics.sql when given no argument (query="${1:-select-basics}") and passes the file to psql with --file.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang@stage-0: scripts/sql/run-query.sh lines 7-11

claims.text: psql --file reads commands from a file; --echo-queries prints each command sent, before its result. --host/--username/--dbname pick server, user and database (a named set of tables on that server); --no-psqlrc skips the system and user start-up files; ON_ERROR_STOP=on stops at the first error.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs, psql reference, Options: -f, -e, -h, -U, -d, -X/--no-psqlrc; Variables: ON_ERROR_STOP

claims.text: psql's default aligned format prints a header line of column names, a dashed separator line, one line per row, and a footer with the row count such as (3 rows), (1 row) or (0 rows).
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs, psql \pset format (aligned) and footer; outputs/stage-0/scripts/sql/run-query.txt

claims.text: Captured output: the first query returns ids 4, 6, 1 (3200000, 1450000, 1250000) with (3 rows); the second 1, 3, 4 with (3 rows); the third shows null_equals_null blank and null_is_null t.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang@stage-0: outputs/stage-0/scripts/sql/run-query.txt

claims.text: PostgreSQL writes boolean true as t and false as f (the boolean type's output function always emits t or f); psql prints that text.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs §8.6 Boolean Type

claims.text: By default psql prints nothing in place of a null value (\pset null is empty), which can be mistaken for an empty string.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs, psql reference, \pset null

claims.text: When you check any query, read the row count first and compare it with the count you expected.
claims.source_hint: Outline item 4

claims.text: WHERE price_vnd <> NULL yields null for every row, so no row is kept: psql prints (0 rows) and no error (transform_null_equals only rewrites = NULL and is off by default).
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs §9.2 Comparison Functions and Operators; §7.2.2; §19.13 transform_null_equals

claims.text: expression IS NOT NULL tests whether a value is not null; expression IS NULL tests whether it is null (NULL IS NULL printed t in the captured run).
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs §9.2 Comparison Functions and Operators (IS NULL / IS NOT NULL predicates)

claims.text: The same query without ORDER BY can return rows in a different order on another copy of the data or on another run with unchanged data (e.g. synchronized sequential scans).
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs §7.5 Sorting Rows (order on disk); §19.13.2 synchronize_seqscans

claims.text: ORDER BY may sort by a column that is not in the SELECT list, since the SELECT list only decides the output columns (section 4, used in section 7); ORDER BY comes before LIMIT; adding ORDER BY price_vnd DESC to the second query returns products 4, 6, 1.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs, SQL Commands: SELECT (Synopsis); §7.5 Sorting Rows; db/seed.sql@stage-0 prices

claims.text: Re-running scripts/up.sh while the lab is up does no harm: dev-secrets.sh creates .env and secrets/lab_key only when missing, and docker compose up recreates a container only if its configuration or image changed, keeping mounted volumes (the db-data rows). It ends by printing The lab is up.
